description: The figure displays a grouping of three pie charts representing the problem distribution based on correctness for "easy," "medium," and "hard" difficulty levels under a "Verify-All" condition. A shared legend on the right indicates four possible categories, each represented by a distinct color: N+K+ (teal), N-K+ (gold), N-K- (orange), and N+K- (red). The "easy" chart contains three visible, labeled slices: teal at 61.5%, gold at 34.6%, and orange at 3.8%. The "medium" chart is divided into four labeled slices: teal at 65.4%, gold at 30.8%, orange at 2.5%, and red at 1.3%. The "hard" chart also contains four labeled slices: gold at 39.6%, orange at 30.6%, teal at 25.1%, and red at 4.7%. Percentage labels are positioned directly inside or immediately adjacent to their respective slices. None of the segments are visually emphasized with exploding, offsetting, or bold text. The slices do not follow a strict descending or ascending size order across all three charts, though the teal and gold segments consistently occupy the largest proportions in the easy and medium charts, while the gold and orange segments are the largest in the hard chart.
